features.feature_value: Their political affiliation and how the comments were worded affected their decisions.
features.evidence_span: "my own political affiliation impacted my response" ... "as well as the way the comments were worded."
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly ties their responses to personal affiliation and perceived wording.

features.feature_value: Profanity/“profan language” led them to reject both, even when they agreed with one part.
features.evidence_span: "The profain language automatically made me reject both arguements"
features.rationale: They describe an automatic rejection rule driven by profane language.

features.feature_value: They suggested removal for posts they felt weren’t healthy for unbiased public contribution.
features.evidence_span: "wasn't healthy for public unbiased contribution and consumption"
features.rationale: They state a specific criterion about protecting unbiased, healthy public discourse.

features.feature_value: They followed their gut/moral compass and removed items that were offensive or that conflicted with their beliefs.
features.evidence_span: "follow my gut" ... "My moral compass came into view" ... "Some were actually offensive" ... "totally did not agree"
features.rationale: They ground decisions in moral beliefs/gut and disagreement offensiveness.

features.feature_value: They removed generic “shit-talking” or middle-school name-calling; kept content that supported constructive discussion.
features.evidence_span: "I generally only removed any that were generic shit-talking instead of constructive conversation" ... "If the comment didn't add anything to a discussion or was just middle school name calling, I'd remove."
features.rationale: They describe a content-based comparison between constructive points vs trolling/name-calling.

features.feature_value: They based decisions on whether the post contributed to discussion or crossed into harmful content (threats/harassment/incitement).
features.evidence_span: "whether the post contributed to political discussion or crossed a line into harmful content such as threats, harassment or incitement."
features.rationale: They provide an explicit line/threshold for harmful content.

features.feature_value: They referenced whether someone would feel negative about it as an influence.
features.evidence_span: "When someone saw it, and felt negative about it."
features.rationale: The criterion is about perceived negative impact on viewers, without specifying other content categories.

features.feature_value: They removed content containing hate speech, found language, or threats; hate is pointless.
features.evidence_span: "If it was hate speech or found language or threats I took them.down" ... "hate is pointless and helps no one"
features.rationale: They explicitly list hate/threat cues as reasons for removal.
